description: Second scenario for the same requirement: VerifyLeader's request channel is buffered, so a verify request can be accepted and then dropped by shutdown; its future must still have a completion path.

harness.description: TestAssuranceVerifyFutureShutdownEscape builds a node with background goroutines disabled, calls VerifyLeader so the request is accepted into its buffered channel, then calls Shutdown and probes the returned future without blocking, reporting whether a response is available, whether the future carries the shutdown escape and whether the caller can complete. A control node served by a running loop performs the same call and reports that it completes.
semantic_changes: Conf.skipStartup is set so no loop can dequeue the verify request, which makes an accepted-then-dropped request deterministic rather than dependent on a shutdown race; Shutdown is called directly on that node.
VerifyLeader's channel is buffered by the library itself (capacity 64), so no extra configuration is needed for the request to be accepted.
The probe reads the future's own fields non-blockingly rather than calling Error(), which would block; this is a state observation of the mechanism, not a timing observation.
The control uses a single-node cluster with a running loop. No target code is modified.

legality.derivation: S23 covers VerifyLeader as well as Apply/Barrier and shows it creating a verifyFuture and sending it to the buffered channel without setting a shutdown escape; S67 shows Error returning only from the response channel or ShutdownCh; S68 shows Shutdown closing the node without draining the channels. The duty and the mechanism are the same as the Apply scenario, which is why this is an independent scenario of one requirement rather than a new question.
legality.applicability: Applies when the verify request was accepted into its buffered channel and the node is then shut down before a loop dequeues it.
unresolved: Whether the remaining future types (configurationChangeFuture, bootstrapFuture, userSnapshotFuture, leadershipTransferFuture) share the gap; their channels are unbuffered or hold one entry, which narrows the window but does not by itself remove it.
Whether the maintainers intend completion after Shutdown not to be guaranteed.
conflicts: The Future.Error documentation lists ErrRaftShutdown among the errors a caller may see, while the verifyFuture has no mechanism to produce it once dropped by shutdown.
alternatives: If completion after Shutdown is deliberately not guaranteed, the correct disposition is a documented caveat rather than wiring an escape.

grounding.derivation: The obligation requires an accepted request's future to remain completable; for VerifyLeader that means a response or the shutdown escape, which is exactly what the event reports from the future the library returned.
grounding.applicability: Evaluated only for an accepted request, declared before the shutdown.

observable_properties.description: An accepted verify request has a completion path after the node shuts down: it was responded, or its future carries the shutdown channel.

uncertainties: Whether the remaining future types share the gap.
Whether the maintainers intend no completion guarantee after Shutdown.
The probe observes the mechanism's state rather than blocking in Error().
